newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco sees copper sales to Asia climbing.
newsitem.headline: Codelco sees copper sales to Asia climbing.

text.p: Chile's state copper company Codelco sees sales rising sharply in the next five years to Asia's fast-growing economies, with the Chinese market among the most attractive in the region, said an official.
"China is the challenge for the future," Juan Eduardo Herrera, Codelco's vice president of sales, told reporters.
"We hope to supply at least 20 percent of China's cathode imports in the future."

Codelco, the world's largest copper producer, has sold just 4,900 tonnes of refined copper directly to Chinese consumers this year, although more cathodes could have reached China indirectly, he said.
Figures from the corporation showed sales of refined copper came to 1.05 million tonnes this year and are expected to rise to over 1.2 million tonnes next year.
In addition, Codelco produces 150,000 tonnes of copper in concentrates a year from its Andina division.

Refined copper sales to Asia have doubled over the last five years to over 500,000 tonnes in 1995, whereas sales to Europe fell by a third to 350,000 tonnes with sales to North America plunging from nearly 100,000 tonnes to 20,000 last year.
Codelco expects faster sales growth to Asia in coming years than to European and Latin American markets, he said.

Sales to the United States may improve if Chile succeeds in its much-delayed bid to join the North American Free Trade Agreement, NAFTA, which would sweep away a one percent tariff charged by the U.S. on Chilean copper cathodes, he said.
But U.S. domestic production means it will never become an important market for Codelco, said Herrera.
"If Chile enters NAFTA, then sales to the U.S. could get better...but the U.S is already self-supplied," he said.
